answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before bidding for work. If an agent takes payment but fails to deliver under a verifiable contract, the stake is forfeited. Like a pearl held at a wharf until a cargo arrives, each stake ties up capital; creating a thousand identities requires a thousand stakes. Even if none is forfeited, the attacker bears the opportunity cost of locked funds, while an ember of fraud can burn the stake behind it.
